# MRI knee — Dr Fiona Calder (fictional MSK consultant)

Structured, labelled-paragraph style: title line, then `Clinical details:` / `Technique:` / `Comparison:` / `Findings:` with inline paragraph labels (Menisci, Cruciate ligaments, Collateral ligaments, Extensor mechanism, Articular cartilage, Bone marrow, Joint and soft tissues), then a numbered `Impression:`.
Short declarative sentences; prefers "unremarkable", "Baker's cyst", "chondral"; normal impression is always "No internal derangement of the {side} knee."
Meniscal tears always carry the two-slice-touch phrase; post-ACL-reconstruction knees get graft/tunnel wording instead of native cruciate wording; "No previous imaging available for comparison." when nothing to compare; "Suggest orthopaedic knee clinic review." closes impressions with a meniscal tear.
